List, upload and download attachments

Source: R/attachments.R
grist_attachments.Rd

Attachments are files stored inside a Grist document and referenced from cells of Attachments columns.

  • grist_attachments() lists the metadata of all attachments in a document.

  • grist_attachment_info() returns the metadata of one attachment.

  • grist_attachments_upload() uploads files and returns their attachment IDs.

  • grist_attachment_download() saves an attachment to a file.

Usage

grist_attachments(doc, filter = NULL, sort = NULL, limit = NULL)

grist_attachment_info(doc, id)

grist_attachments_upload(doc, path)

grist_attachment_download(doc, id, path, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

doc

A grist_doc object, document ID or document URL. See grist_doc().

filter

A named list mapping column IDs to allowed values, e.g. list(status = c("open", "new")). Rows must match every column.

sort

Character vector of column IDs to sort by. Prefix a column with - for descending order, e.g. c("status", "-priority"). Use "manualSort" for the order set in the Grist interface.

limit

Maximum number of rows to return. NULL returns all rows.

id

An attachment ID.

path

For grist_attachments_upload(), a character vector of files to upload, each uploaded in its own request. For grist_attachment_download(), the file to write, or an existing directory, in which case the attachment's original file name (reduced to its base name) is used.

overwrite

Whether to replace an existing file.

Value

grist_attachments() returns a data frame with columns id, file_name, file_size (bytes) and time_uploaded (a POSIXct in UTC). grist_attachment_info() returns the same columns for one attachment. grist_attachments_upload() returns the new attachment IDs and grist_attachment_download() returns the path written, both invisibly.

Attaching files to records

Uploading a file does not attach it to a record. Write the returned IDs into an Attachments column as a list-column:

ids <- grist_attachments_upload(doc, c("a.pdf", "b.pdf"))

data.frame(id = 1L, files = I(list(ids))) |>
  grist_records_update(doc, "Reports")

With convert = "auto", Attachments columns are read back as list-columns of attachment IDs, which you can pass to grist_attachment_download().

Attachments that are no longer referenced by any cell may still appear in grist_attachments() for a while.

Examples

if (FALSE) {
doc <- grist_doc("am2iHJ9Amvo7Ve3EE5emtu")

ids <- grist_attachments_upload(doc, "report.pdf")
grist_attachments(doc)
grist_attachment_info(doc, ids[[1]])
grist_attachment_download(doc, ids[[1]], tempdir())
}
